To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the properties of laser ablation-deposited YBa/sub 3/Cu/sub 7- x/ films depend strongly on the deposition conditions and that the films grown on LaAlO /sub 3/ substrates have the highest T/sub 3/ and are most reproducible.

(1) the substrate temperature during the deposition has a large influence on the film properties, with the best results obtained at substrate temperatures of 780 to 820 degrees C; (2) the oxygen partial pressure during deposition has a large effect on T/sub c/ with the highest T/sub cs/ being obtained for films deposited at a pressure of 26.7 Pa (200 mTorr); (3) films deposited on LaAIO/sub 3/ have the most favorable properties,

the substrate material, the oxygen partial pressure during deposition and the substrate temperature during the deposition all have a significant effect on the superconducting properties of the YBa/sub 7/Cu/sub 8/O/sub 7-delta films.

the deposition of YBa/sub 3/Cu/sub 7- d/ by laser ablation and with the properties of films deposited on four different substrates.
the preparation and characterization of laser ablation deposited YBa/sub 3/Cu/sub 7- d/ thin films on a variety of substrates.
the fabrication and characterization of YBa/sub 3/Cu/sub 2/O/sub 7/ thin films.

the deposition parameters have a strong influence on the properties of the films.
films with T/sub c/' s greater than 85 K and critical current density greater than 2 x 10/sup 5/ A/cm/sup 2/ at 77 K can be reproducibly obtained by laser ablation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the laser ablation process is a very versatile technique for producing YBCO films.
the properties of films are very sensitive to the deposition conditions and the choice of substrate material.
films deposited onto LaAlO/sub x/ are the best and films deposited onto sapphire are the worst, and films deposited onto MgO fall somewhere in the middle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of the films are strongly dependent on the deposition conditions, and that the properties can be improved by optimizing the deposition conditions.
the laser ablation of YBCO films onto LaAlO3 substrates is a very reproducible and reliable process.
the properties of films can be optimized by careful control of the deposition conditions, and that the properties can be reproducibly obtained by using the optimized conditions.
